title: Level 3 (Advanced) - A-12
notes:
West leads the ♦10 against 5♠. South must avoid losing 2 diamond tricks and the ♣A. Dummy's clubs can be established to provide discards for South's diamond losers. South must make sure that the defenders cannot take 2 diamond tricks first.

West's lead of the ♦10 marks East with the ♦J and ♦A and West with short diamonds. If West has a singleton diamond nothing can be done. The defense will get a diamond ruff. If West has 2 diamonds and the ♣A, South must play dummy's ♦Q at trick 1. If East ducks South's ♦K will prevent the defense from taking more than 1 diamond trick.

If East wins the ♦A, he cannot attack diamonds from his side of the table without giving up a trick to the ♦9. South must be careful to win a heart shift with the ♥A to preserve the ♥K as an entry to dummy's clubs.

If South errs by playing low from dummy at trick 1, East will also play low. South will win the ♦K, but when West wins the ♣A he can play another diamond through dummy's holding. East will be able to take 2 diamond tricks.
